### Introduction

To understand certain topics better, science classes are divided into different areas:

AreaExamples
HumanitiesPhilosophy, History, Literature
ExactPhysics, Mathematics, Chemistry
BiologicalZoology, Genetics, Biochemistry

Table 1: Example of sciences organized into different areas.

We agree with this approach. But we know it can make people think the sciences are completely independent from each other. This can create barriers to learning.

Because of this, we chose to build an **interdisciplinary** project. It uses a teaching model that considers different types of intelligence.

### On Knowledge

#### What is the knowledge level?

One of the best definitions of our level of knowledge was given by Socrates thousands of years ago
• "I neither know nor think that I know"

Reflection 1: On Our Knowledge

What conclusion can we draw from Socrates' statement?

At first, we can see this as an analogy. Our knowledge is an empty circle that needs to be filled. But this idea has a problem: it says human knowledge has a limited size.

A more realistic view is this: as we gain knowledge and fill the circle, we discover new knowledge. The circle grows.

Imagine you want to learn something new. Now, move your cursor (or your finger, if you are reading on a smartphone) over Figure 1. Watch the circle grow. This is what happens in real life: the more we learn, the more we see there is still much to learn.
Figure 1: Visual representation of a person's knowledge.

#### How Do We Learn?

For a long time, people thought the ability to learn was linked to only one type of intelligence. This idea changed at the end of the 20th century with the **Theory of Multiple Intelligences** by Howard Gardner.

Thanks to his work, we now understand that there are different types of intelligence. Each person can develop different thinking abilities. Chart 1 shows the nine types of intelligence, as explained by Sabriye Şener and Ayten Çokçalışkan
Chart 1: Chart showing the types of intelligence. While they are presented uniformly, each person develops them at different levels.

text.text:
- **Verbal-linguistic:** Ability to express oneself effectively through speech and writing.
- **Logical-mathematical:** Capacity to perform calculations and understand situations systematically and logically.
- **Visual-spatial:** Aptitude for perceiving, modifying, and creating images and spaces.
- **Musical:** Ability to recognize tones, rhythms, and the emotional aspects of music.
- **Bodily-kinesthetic:** Skill in using the body and its movements with precision.
- **Intrapersonal:** Capacity to recognize and understand one's own emotions and motivations.
- **Interpersonal:** Ability to understand and interact effectively with others.
- **Naturalistic:** Sensitivity to classify and comprehend elements of the natural world.
- **Existential:** Capacity to reflect on philosophical and abstract questions, such as the meaning of life.

Reflection 2: On Our Intelligence

How would you assess your levels of intelligence according to Gardner’s theory?

#### Artificial Intelligence?

Every day, this tool grows quickly, especially among the public. But is it really intelligent?

Dr. Sabine Hossenfelder shows, in videos on her channel and in her weekly newsletter, some problems with the AI models we use today (<htcite0>). Among them, we point out the work of Jan Betley and his team. They showed that algorithms can make harmful information and act in a misleading way (<htcite1>).
Another important point is to understand the definition of "artificial intelligence" (<htcite0>):
• "an area of computer science that deals with giving machines the ability to seem like they have human intelligence."

This definition says AI seems to have human intelligence. So we are not talking about full intelligence. AI is very different from human intelligence.

AI has limits and its algorithms have flaws. But AI is still a valuable technology. We just need to use it with care.

### Learning Steps

#### The First Years

When we are children, we cannot stop asking questions. This helps our thinking to develop (<htcite0>). But as we grow up, some people stop asking questions. They change their habits and look for "solid" answers (truths) that are often too simple. Because of this, they stop questioning and start to accept information without thinking about it. Recent studies suggest that these "solid answers" are linked to relativism. Relativism stops these answers from being accepted as unquestionable truths (<htcite1>).

source.text: Chouinard, M. M., Harris, P. L., & Maratsos, M. P.

#### From School to University

We learn every day and knowledge has no limits. But there is a time in our lives when we go to kindergarten, to school, and, in some cases, to university.

Reflection 3: On Access to Education

Should everyone have the right to attend university?

Dr. Francisco A. González Redondo talks about the history of mathematics. He explains how science is divided and the path students follow in their studies. In their early years, students learn pre-mathematics through examples. Later, they learn proto-mathematics. Finally, when they enter university, they develop a deeper understanding of mathematics
Mathematics is the base of all sciences, including the humanities. So we can use Dr. Francisco A. González Redondo's conclusions for all sciences (<htcite0>), like this:

Pre-SciencesProto-SciencesSciences
Initial contact with sciences, using everyday examples.Presentation of content without the necessary tools to understand it deeply, but with the minimum required to understand the world around them. In some rare cases, students also have access to labs.In-depth study of sciences, understanding the tools and foundations of each field.

### Conclusion

In this introduction, we saw that there are different types of intelligence. We also saw that, often, people do not really understand the sciences. They only get a first, simple introduction to them.

To help students and teachers, **History Tracers** is making tools and content. These tools help people use their intelligence to understand science better.
